nodes.name: Reunite Branches

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per draft (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

# Summarize long emails for captions

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers captions work end to end across Google Sheets, Telegram and Slack.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. On Telegram Event
2. Stamp & Shape Draft
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Classify with AI
6. Groq Chat Model
7. Store as Urgent
8. Store as Routine
9. Store as FYI
10. Alert Slack — Other
11. Reunite Branches
12. Fingerprint for Idempotency
13. Drop Already-Processed Items
14. Load Previous Snapshot
15. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
16. Stamp Completion Time
17. Persist Run Metadata
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
20. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing captions work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

On Telegram Event → Stamp & Shape Draft → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Classify with AI → Groq Chat Model → Store as Urgent → Store as Routine → Store as FYI → Alert Slack — Other → Reunite Branches → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Telegram aligned by hand for captions
- Pushing captions events into Google Sheets and Telegram the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Captions work where "Stamp & Shape Draft" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Captions work that only reaches Google Sheets when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Telegram in step for captions, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Telegram are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this captions build
- A failed Google Sheets or Telegram call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this captions build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a captions run reports once rather than 23 times
- Every captions run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; Groq API key; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

One Text Classifier node replaces what would otherwise be a chain of brittle IF/Switch keyword checks — the LLM handles the ambiguous cases a rules engine can't. Each category gets its own action node, so a failure in one branch (say, a bad Slack call) never blocks the others; Merge reunites them so the run still reports one clean completion.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Add a 4th category with its own action branch.
2. Replace one action (e.g. a Slack ping) with a task-creation node and see how the wiring changes.
3. Feed the classifier deliberately ambiguous text and check which fallback category it lands in.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Telegram bot token**
Same bot token as the Telegram node (@BotFather → /newbot).
_Gotcha:_ A bot supports only one webhook at a time — a second workflow listening on the same bot steals the updates.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your captions process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole captions payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.
